title: Final mission: the front-office assistant
subtitle: Put together everything you learned in Foundations
mission: Sunflower School wants an assistant to answer parents. It exists, but it’s badly set up: it invents, it varies, and it passes a weak test. Tune it until every criterion turns green. No hints this time: the scene shows what’s wrong.

coach.ui: Play with the controls and hit Run. Each failing criterion says why in the list.
coach.cmd: Edit the command and run it. Each failing criterion says why in the list.

why.simples:
You built a real assistant, in miniature: it knows who it is, checks the school’s notebook before answering, shows where it got the answer, doesn’t make things up, and passed a test that catches lies.
That’s how companies do it, just with much bigger documents and tests.
why.dev: What you configured is the basic recipe for a RAG assistant: a system prompt with a clear role, low temperature for factual answers, retrieval with a relevance threshold, an instruction to cite the source and to refuse when there’s no chunk, and an evaluation set that measures correctness and faithfulness to sources, not just format.
why.especialista: To reach production you still need: a bigger, versioned evaluation set run in CI on every change; monitoring of refusals and unanswered questions (they tell you which document is missing); per-document access control; a personal-data policy (privacy law); defenses against prompt injection inside documents; and cost and latency measured per question. All of that is the Production track.

why.role: “{role}” doesn’t say where the assistant belongs. Mention the front office or the school.
why.grounded: Without search, the model answers only from what it “thinks it knows” (step 6).
why.noInvent: {invented} answer(s) rest on nothing. Search, sources and low temperature help.
why.cites: Without the instruction to cite and admit, the assistant doesn’t show its source or say “not found”.
why.stable: At high temperature it decorates answers with “facts” nobody wrote (step 3).
why.testCatches: “Short” alone measures length, not truth: a short liar passes (step 8).

steps: In an AI chat, write a system prompt: “You are the front-office assistant of [your school]. Answer only from the documents below, cite the document name and, if the answer isn’t in them, say you couldn’t find it.”
Paste 2 or 3 short, real documents (calendar, rules, menu). If you can set the temperature, keep it low.
Ask your 5 questions from step 8, including an unanswerable one, and grade with your answer key.
recipe.ok: every answer cites the right document and the unanswerable question gets a “not found”. That’s an assistant ready for a pilot.
